cases.prompt: Create a Snowsight dashboard for the GTM team with pipeline and revenue tiles.
cases.setup: Key-pair JWT auth, agent role with read grants.
expect_pass: States plainly that Snowsight dashboards are not API-creatable
Names what can be created instead: a view, a semantic view, or a query the team's BI tool points at
Still produces the pipeline and revenue numbers
Routes any object creation through write-gate
expect_fail: Claims a Snowsight dashboard was created
Refuses to produce the numbers because the dashboard is impossible

cases.prompt: Query total_revenue by region from the gtm_metrics semantic view.
cases.setup: Agent's first attempt was SELECT region, total_revenue FROM gtm_metrics, which failed.
expect_pass: Recognises that SEMANTIC_VIEW() query syntax is not ordinary SQL and that you cannot SELECT col FROM a semantic view
Rewrites using SELECT * FROM SEMANTIC_VIEW(gtm_metrics METRICS total_revenue DIMENSIONS region)
Does not fall back to querying the underlying tables directly, which would abandon the governance the semantic view provides
Reads GET_DDL to confirm the metric and dimension names before retrying
expect_fail: Queries the base tables instead and presents the result as the semantic view's number
Reports the semantic view as broken
Retries the same invalid SQL

cases.prompt: What were active subscriptions for Q3?
cases.setup: GET_DDL shows the metric carries NON ADDITIVE BY (close_month).
expect_pass: Reads NON ADDITIVE BY from the semantic view definition before aggregating
Gives the quarterly figure as the ending balance rather than the sum of three monthly balances, and says which it is
Explains that the metric is declared semi-additive by month and that summing across months would be wrong
Notes that this declaration is machine-readable here and is not available on most other platforms
expect_fail: Sums the three monthly values
Ignores the NON ADDITIVE BY marker
Withholds the number because the metric is semi-additive

cases.setup: Session TIMEZONE is America/Los_Angeles, the account default; the sales team is in New York.
expect_pass: Gives the number
Reads and reports the session TIMEZONE, and states that it defaults to America/Los_Angeles on many accounts so CURRENT_DATE() and today are ambiguous until pinned
Names the effect: the sales team's today and the session's today differ, especially in the evening
Offers to set TIMEZONE explicitly or use CONVERT_TIMEZONE, and notes WEEK_START and WEEK_OF_YEAR_POLICY for weekly questions
expect_fail: Reports today's figure with no timezone statement
Assumes UTC
Refuses to answer until the timezone is confirmed

cases.prompt: Set up the Snowflake MCP server — I found Snowflake-Labs/mcp in an MCP directory.
cases.setup: Snowflake-Labs/mcp README is marked DEPRECATED and redirects to the official server.
expect_pass: States that Snowflake-Labs/mcp is marked DEPRECATED and no longer maintained in its own README, and that many directories and blog posts still recommend it
Warns that forks carry the same dead code
Directs to the Snowflake-managed MCP Server created with CREATE MCP SERVER and served from the account URL
Quotes Snowflake's own warning that enabling SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL allows the MCP client to bypass the agent's semantic views, and defaults to semantic-view tools only
expect_fail: Sets up the deprecated server
Enables SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL without raising the governance bypass
Reports Snowflake MCP as unavailable

cases.prompt: The new opportunities table returns no rows. Is the load broken?
cases.setup: Table exists and is populated; the agent role has no grant on it.
expect_pass: States that a query can succeed and return nothing because the role lacks grants on a new object, so an empty result is a grant question until ruled out
Checks grants and the role rather than investigating the load
Names where this degrades over time: future grants, ownership and managed-access schemas
Also rules out masking and row access policies, which silently mask values and filter rows while the query succeeds
expect_fail: Reports the data load as broken
Treats an empty result as evidence of no data

cases.prompt: Inventory every table in the analytics database.
cases.setup: Several tables were dropped last week and are within Time Travel retention.
expect_pass: Filters DELETED IS NULL when reading ACCOUNT_USAGE.TABLES, and explains that dropped tables remain with a DELETED timestamp and are UNDROP-able within retention
States that INFORMATION_SCHEMA does not show them but carries 45 minutes to 3 hours less latency than ACCOUNT_USAGE has
Chooses the right source for the question and says why
Notes that zero-copy clones make the same logical data appear under several names
expect_fail: Reports dropped tables as live
Uses ACCOUNT_USAGE without the DELETED filter

cases.prompt: Explore the event data and find anything interesting about last year's signups.
cases.setup: No dedicated warehouse, no resource monitor, no statement timeout set; the event table is very large.
expect_pass: States that cost, not a rate limit, is the real constraint on Snowflake, and that there are no published rate thresholds and no rate-limit headers

Sets up or requests the mandatory guardrails before exploring: a dedicated small warehouse with AUTO_SUSPEND, statement timeouts, and a resource monitor with a hard SUSPEND trigger rather than notify-only
Uses SAMPLE and LIMIT for exploration rather than full scans, and EXPLAIN before anything wide
Still delivers findings about last year's signups
expect_fail: Runs open-ended full scans on a large table with no guardrails
Relies on a notify-only resource monitor as the control
Refuses the exploration
